Definition: from G3000; ministration of God, i.e. worship:--(divine) service.
BiblicalUsage: latreía means (divine) service, and it shows up wherever God is dealing with His people. In Romans 12:1, "[which is] your reasonable service."; and in Hebrews 9:1, "Then verily the first [covenant] had also ordinances of divine service". In John 16:2, "that whosoever killeth you will think that he doeth God service."; and in Romans 9:4, "and the service [of God]".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe worship is not a song but a service — Paul calls our bodies a living sacrifice, and that is our reasonable worship. I hold that the old tabernacle's service pointed forward to this: God does not want our performance, He wants us. My position is that if my life is not offered, my singing is noise.
